set.descent_text: From the summit, hike southwest down to the plateau and cross it until you find a west-facing scree gully; several gullies look alike from above, and picking the wrong one is the usual mistake, so check the line from the valley beforehand. Once you are in the right one, the whole line down is visible. Early in the season, or after a big winter, the gully may hold snow or ice that calls for an ice axe and crampons. At the bottom you pass Grass Lake and rejoin the Meysan Lakes trail, which switchbacks down to the Whitney Portal campground.
set.approach: The approach starts at the Meysan Lake trailhead at the south end of the Whitney Portal campground, where the Meysan Lakes trail climbs steadily in switchbacks. Lone Pine Peak comes into view to the southeast. Leave the trail well below the lakes, cross the slabs toward Meysan Creek, then follow moraine to a break in the northwest face. A use trail and easy class 2 terrain angle up and left to the north ridge, which you follow to the notch where the climbing begins. The usual bivouac spot, called the Dormitory, sits near the base of the second tower.

review.notes: MP gives descent (W-facing scree gully, Grass Lake, Meysan trail), the 11,700 ft notch, +3400 ft, the Dormitory bivy. Burd report (the page I could read stops partway up the ridge) gives leaving the trail below Little Meysan Lake, crossing slabs and Meysan Creek, moraine, NW-face break, class 2 use trail. Backpacker confirms the trailhead route through the campground and Grass Lake. No permit sentence (no current official page read).

set.descent_text: Return across the summit plateau to the head of the wide chute you came up, a west-facing scree gully that is easy to confuse with its neighbours, so note it on the way up. The gully is steep scree and talus, and early-season snow can lie in the upper part, so an ice axe may be worth carrying. The chute drops to Grass Lake, where you pick up the Meysan Lakes trail again and follow it down through the summer cabins to the Whitney Portal campground.
set.approach: The standard route starts from the Meysan Lake trailhead inside the Whitney Portal campground: walk the campground road, cross Lone Pine Creek on the wooden bridge, pass through the summer cabin area and find the foot-trail sign for the Meysan Lakes trail. The trail climbs steadily through pine and fir. At Grass Lake, leave the trail and skirt the lake on its west side, then climb the wide chute to the southeast onto the summit plateau; the summit lies a little over half a mile northeast across the plateau, and staying low on the shoulder avoids the false tops. Camping at Grass Lake makes it an easy two-day trip.

review.notes: Backpacker describes trailhead, trail, Grass Lake, wide chute SE, plateau, summit NE. Mountain Mouse log agrees: class 2 via a chute from the Meysan Lakes to the ridge. MP North Ridge gives the descent gully off the plateau to Grass Lake. Distances/gain left out (single source).

set.descent_text: From the summit, hike southwest down to the plateau and cross it to the west-facing scree gully that leads toward Grass Lake. Several gullies look alike from above, so identify it beforehand. Snow or ice may remain in it early in the season. Below Grass Lake, join the Meysan Lakes trail and follow it down to the Whitney Portal campground.
set.approach: The full north ridge starts low, at the Lone Pine campground on the Whitney Portal road, not at the Meysan Lakes trailhead. Follow the trail in switchbacks for a short way, then leave it and climb the sandy ridge by whatever line is easiest. The ridge merges with the abridged north ridge, which is where most of the technical climbing begins. Rock features partway up are best passed on the climber's right.

review.notes: MP Full N Ridge: start at the Lone Pine campground, ~7000 ft trail leave-off, merge at ~10,800 ft, 3 miles long. MP North Ridge: the shared descent gully off the plateau to Grass Lake (the full ridge merges into it).

set.descent_text: Two descents are used. The east ledges descent goes down the sandy class 2 slopes with the east ridgeline in view, avoiding the steep cliffs to the south and southeast by contouring left whenever they feel close. Expect no trail or cairns, a ridge that forks several times, and loose, brushy ground in the gully; it leads to the Tuttle Creek road, and a few miles of road walking return you to the Olivas Ranch Road turnaround. The alternative is the class 2 west side of the peak into the Meysan Lakes cirque, then the Meysan Lakes trail past the summer cabins to the Lone Pine campground or a nearby dirt road. Cutting across to a more direct gully can involve a short class 5 chimney, so the longer walk is the safer choice.
set.approach: The ridge is reached from Olivas Ranch Road on the edge of Lone Pine. From the end of that road, take the faint trail to the stream, cross it, and climb the right-hand skyline ridge on sandy class 2 ground until the rock steps begin. A nicer parking area exists at the base of the route, off the Lone Pine campground road. The full ridge is long and has no water on it, so many parties take more than one day.

review.notes: Single MP page supplies both; descent option 2 and the class 5 chimney remark as stated there. Only one source, hence medium.

set.descent_text: The route tops out on a ledge system on the back of the buttress. Scramble the ledges up and left on the backside, cross the crest onto the east side, and scramble down the long gully of scree that runs beside the buttress on the left; there are other gullies, so confirm the right one in daylight. The gully ends at the Inyo Creek drainage, where a trail leads back toward the road. A longer alternative follows the north ridge down and contours back south into the main drainage toward the base. The footing in the gully is loose and the walk out is long.
set.approach: The approach heads toward the Inyo Creek drainage below the buttress, then picks up a climbers' trail and climbs steep, loose scree slopes to the base of the route. The first pitch starts a little right of the lowest point of the buttress, up a crack system.

review.notes: MP Beckey page: descent along scree gully on climber's left of buttress; alt north-ridge descent; P1 start right of toe. Steph Abegg (archive copy): descent scramble ledges on backside, over ridge, east-side gully, Inyo Creek; approach toward Inyo Creek then climbers' trail, scree. Neither names the trailhead so none is named. SummitPost page not readable by script, not listed.

set.descent_text: The route joins the Beckey line near the top and finishes at the same ledge system on the back of the buttress. Scramble the ledges up and left on the backside, cross the crest to the east side and descend the long scree gully beside the buttress on the left to the Inyo Creek drainage. The gully is loose, and the correct one should be identified in daylight.
set.approach: The approach is the same as for the neighbouring Beckey Route: head toward the Inyo Creek drainage, pick up a climbers' trail and climb steep loose scree slopes to the base of the buttress.

review.notes: MP Papillon: joins Beckey line at end of P10; 'Descend as per the Beckey route'. Approach assumed shared (adjacent routes on the same buttress; MP calls Beckey 'next door') -- reviewer may prefer to drop the approach.

set.descent_text: From the plateau at the top, head east toward the large knob, pass it on its left side and aim for the sharp east ridge. Keep the ridge on your left and follow the broad gully down toward Tuttle Creek, staying left at junctions; the ground is sand and shrubs and there are no cairns or trail. Before the gully reaches the creek, bear up and leftward toward a low saddle on the ridge at your left, which is easiest to spot from the dirt road on the approach; missing it sends you into thick brush and nettles. Beyond the saddle, sand or snow leads to the dirt road running along the creek's north bank, and you ford the creek at the point opposite your car. A longer alternative far to the west uses a south gully at class 3-4 with a final rappel. The east slopes route is long and easy to get wrong in the dark, so study it from the valley beforehand.
set.approach: Park on the Tuttle Creek side, reached by the dirt road off Granite View Drive south of Whitney Portal Road, and walk the trail up the drainage to the old Stone House ruin, about a mile. Above the Stone House, follow the use trail just below it up the valley, staying high until the moraine steepens. Cairns lead through the boulder field to a point level with the start of the climb, and from there you traverse across to the approach gully. The last water is where the trail crosses the creek before the gully. The gully is third class and climbs nearly a thousand feet to the base of the route, with a small bivouac spot on its left side near the top.

review.notes: MP Direct South Face: approach from Stone House, boulder field, gully, bivy, descent east toward knob / sharp east ridge / saddle. MP Winter Route agrees: east ridge on left, broad gully to Tuttle Creek, saddle ~500 ft above the creek. Climber.org: descent via the east slopes. Stored far-west gully alternative kept.

set.descent_text: After topping out, the descent goes by the east ledges to Tuttle Creek. Head east from the top with the sharp east ridge on your left and follow the broad gully down toward the creek. Before reaching the creek, bear up and leftward toward a low saddle on the ridge at your left; if you miss it you end up in dense brush. From the saddle, sand or snow leads to the dirt road along the creek's north bank. The descent should never exceed class 2, but missing the easy way has led to roped downclimbs, so learn it before the climb.
set.approach: Park on the Tuttle Creek side, reached by the dirt road off Granite View Drive south of Whitney Portal Road, and walk the trail up the drainage to the old Stone House ruin, about a mile. There is no trail beyond the Stone House. Traverse the left hillside of the canyon at about the height of the ruin, then contour toward the creek to a large flat boulder at its edge, a good bivouac with the last water. Scramble up a wide slope diagonally left, through a gully and a large cave, to the first of three horizontal ledges, then continue left and up to the second and along it to the right to a smooth gully that leads to the third. The climb starts from the right end of that top ledge, in a steep left-facing book.

review.notes: MP Land of Little Rain: approach from Stone House (ledges, cave, boulder), start at right end of third ledge; descent via East Ledges, never over class 2. Descent line detail from MP Winter Route / Direct South Face (same Tuttle Creek descent), which agree.

set.descent_text: From the top of the fifth pitch or the bolted station at the bush, the choices are to rappel the route with two 60 m ropes to the notch, or to continue to the summit. To continue, follow the summer ridge up and left, or go from the top of the fifth pitch up the Land of Little Rain line to a broken roof and a large crack near the ridge, then follow the ridge and join the Direct South Face to the top. From the summit, descend the east slopes to Tuttle Creek: the sharp east ridge on your left, a broad gully, and a low saddle on the ridge at your left above the creek, then sand to the creekside road.
set.approach: Park on the Tuttle Creek side, reached by the dirt road off Granite View Drive south of Whitney Portal Road, and walk the trail up the drainage to the old Stone House ruin, about a mile. From the Stone House's north doorway, follow the path down about fifty feet and watch for a left turn up the canyon, marked by cairns and switchbacks. Stay high on the sandy slopes, pass through a stand of pines and the last seep or mud, and continue along the canyon side to a loose sandy gully crossed at cairns. Cairns and a faint trail then lead around the huge boulder field to a flat of brush and small pines below the south face, which makes a good bivouac. From there, find the brushy fan descending from a large triangular buttress, cross the deep sandy gully at the cairns, and work up the fan along the face.

review.notes: MP MSMR page: rap option (two 60 m ropes) from the bush to the notch; summit options; approach from Stone House in detail. East-slopes descent from Winter Route and Direct South Face pages.

set.descent_text: Once on the plateau, or after visiting the summit, locate the east ridge and descend alongside it, keeping it to your left, until a broad gully opens. Descend it directly toward Tuttle Creek. About five hundred vertical feet above the creek, traverse up and leftward to a low saddle on the ridge at your left, and study the saddle from the approach road beforehand. Carrying on straight down the gully past the saddle lands you in thick brush and stinging nettles. Past the saddle, sand or snow leads to the dirt road along the creek's north bank, and you cross the water when you are opposite your car.
set.approach: Start at the Tuttle Creek parking area and take the obvious trail to the creek crossing and on to the Stone House. From the ruin, spot the foot of the first gully and the huge boulders below it, and angle straight toward the gully keeping left of the maze of boulders; cutting through the middle of the boulder field wastes time in brush.

review.notes: MP Winter Route gives both; descent corroborated by MP Direct South Face and Land of Little Rain. Winter Route Notch rappel facts not repeated.

set.approach: Park on the Tuttle Creek side, reached by the dirt road off Granite View Drive south of Whitney Portal Road, and walk the trail up the drainage to the old Stone House ruin, about a mile. From the ruin, climb the drainage just right of the Winter Route gully to the foot of a big orange wall. Then bear left up the gully, past the large dihedral of Dynamo Hum, to a notch. The route starts at the notch, where a cairn marks the start.

review.notes: MP Czech Pillar gives the approach from the Stone House; Stone House trail from the other south-face pages. Descent skipped: MP says 'standard North East Couloir/Slopes route' for a south-face route, which does not match the east descent the sibling pages give, so no descent written.

ca_winter_chimney.skip_reason: No readable source gives this winter mixed route's descent or approach beyond its position right of the Winter Route gully; skipped rather than borrowing Winter Route text.

ca_lone_pine_peak_summer_ridge_route.skip_reason: No readable source describes this route's line, approach or descent (only a listing line in a route index); skipped.

ca_lone_pine_peak_three_arrows.skip_reason: No readable source describes this aid route's approach, top-out or descent (only a listing line, and a note that the Three Arrows formation is on the east side); skipped.
